installation.title: Install Anatomy
installation.summary: Start from a release package and run your first structure check in under a minute.

blocks.0: The npm package is named anatomy-cli; after installation, use the anatomy command everywhere. Choose the installation method that matches your environment.
blocks.7: After installation, run anatomy --help to confirm the command is available. Release packages require Node.js 18+; source development requires Bun 1.3+.

quick-start.title: Your first check
quick-start.summary: Give Anatomy a target directory and run a structure check immediately.

blocks.0: Place anatomy.json in the target directory or any parent, then pass the directory directly to anatomy. With no target, Anatomy checks the current directory.

ci.title: CI integration
ci.summary: Stable exit codes and JSON output make structure checks a natural part of every pull request.

blocks.0: Exit code 0 means the target conforms to the definition, 1 means a block finding exists, and 2 means a runtime error or invalid definition.

cli.title: Commands and options
cli.summary: The complete CLI option reference and common combinations.

1: target: Directory to check, defaults to the current directory.
--target, -t: Alternative to the positional target argument.
--format: human or json, defaults to human.
--ignore: Comma-separated names; can be passed more than once.

output.title: Output and exit codes
output.summary: Human output is suited to local inspection; JSON output is suited to archiving and automation.

blocks.1: The default output shows whether the check conforms, the finding count, and the path and message for every finding.
5: 0: conforms is true; the check passed.
1: At least one block finding; merging should be blocked.
2: Runtime error or invalid definition; fix the configuration and retry.

anatomy.title: Anatomy concepts
anatomy.summary: Describe repository structure with a versioned JSON definition.

blocks.0: Anatomy compares a structure definition with the deterministic file tree of the target directory, checking names, nesting, quantities, one-of rules, and policies.
1: Names: whether a file or directory is named correctly.
Nesting: whether an entry sits under the expected parent directory.
Quantities: whether required, optional, or bounded entries meet their constraints.
one-of: whether exactly one allowed structure was selected from multiple candidates.
Policies: whether a finding is marked block, warn, or allow.

definition.title: Definition example
definition.summary: Start with a minimal definition for a service directory.

blocks.1: The default definition file is anatomy.json. Place it in the target directory or any parent and Anatomy selects the closest one; use --definition to name a different file explicitly.

contributing.title: Repository layout and development
contributing.summary: Understand the roles of the CLI, engine, schema, and definition packages in the monorepo.

0: apps/anatomy-cli: CLI entry point, argument parsing, and filesystem adapters.
packages/anatomy: Anatomy tree utilities and the conformance engine.
packages/schemas: Runtime schemas for Anatomy Draft.
